title: Create a `Map<Long, String>` of employee id → employee name.
shortTitle: Create a Map<Long, String> of employee id to employee name

s1_definition.profdef: `Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)` builds a `Map` by applying a key function and a value function to each element. For id to name you pass `Employee::getId` as the key mapper and `Employee::getName` as the value mapper.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya has a pile of employee files and wants a quick phone-book style lookup: give an employee id and get back the name. She makes an index where each id points to one name.
s1_definition.oneliner: `toMap(Employee::getId, Employee::getName)` turns a list of employees into an id-to-name lookup map.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)` builds a `Map` by applying a key function and a value function to each element. For id to name you pass `Employee::getId` as the key mapper and `Employee::getName` as the value mapper.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Priya has a pile of employee files and wants a quick phone-book style lookup: give an employee id and get back the name. She makes an index where each id points to one name.

**One line to remember:** `toMap(Employee::getId, Employee::getName)` turns a list of employees into an id-to-name lookup map.

sections.s2_technical:
`stream().collect(Collectors.toMap(Employee::getId, Employee::getName))` iterates each employee, uses the id as the map key, and uses the name as the value. Ids are expected to be unique, so each key appears once. The result is a `HashMap` by default, giving constant-time lookups by id.

If two employees share the same id, the two-argument toMap throws an `IllegalStateException` because it does not know which value to keep. That is actually a useful safety net: it surfaces a data integrity problem rather than silently discarding a record. If duplicates are legitimately possible, you supply a third merge-function argument to resolve them.

The senior nuance is to be deliberate about the map implementation and null-handling. `toMap` rejects null values by throwing, and the default HashMap has no ordering; if you need ordering or a specific type you pass a fourth map-supplier argument. For an id-keyed lookup, uniqueness is the contract, so the default two-argument form is the correct and intention-revealing choice.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — A service at the National Bank of India must resolve employee names from their ids many times per request, and repeatedly scanning the list would be slow.

This is exactly what toMap solves — it builds an id-to-name index once so each later lookup is constant time, and it fails loudly if two records share an id.

The code defines a `DirectoryService.idToName` method and a demo.
sections.s5_journey:
Input: three employees with ids 101, 102, 103 and names Rajesh, Priya, Amit.

Step 1: The stream visits each employee in turn.

Step 2: toMap takes the id as key and the name as value, inserting each pair into a HashMap.

Step 3: Because ids are unique, no collision occurs and all three entries are stored.

Step 4: A lookup of id 102 returns Priya in constant time.

```
INFO: id 102 → Priya
INFO: full index = {101=Rajesh, 102=Priya, 103=Amit}
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Employee Name Lookup ═══

  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ──O(1) get──→ name
  │ staff    │→│ DirectoryService │
  │ list     │ │ toMap(id→name)   │
  └──────────┘ └──────────────────┘
     build index once, lookup many times
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Collectors.toMap (id→name) ═══

  ┌─ toMap two-arg form ───────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper) → HashMap                    │
  │ duplicate key → IllegalStateException (safety net)         │
  │ null value → NullPointerException                          │
  │ need merge → 3-arg; need ordered/typed map → 4-arg supplier│
  │ HashMap → O(1) average lookup by id                        │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │        DirectoryService       │
  │  + idToName(List): Map<Long,…>│ toMap(getId, getName)
  └───────────────────────────────┘

  Call chain:
  1. stream()
  2. collect(toMap(getId, getName))
  3. map.get(id) → name
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To build an id-to-name lookup I collect the employee stream with Collectors toMap, passing a key mapper that extracts the id and a value mapper that extracts the name. The result is a HashMap by default, which gives me constant-time lookups by id, so a service that resolves names many times per request at the National Bank of India builds the index once and then reads from it cheaply.

Because ids are supposed to be unique, each key appears exactly once. If two employees happen to share an id, the two-argument toMap throws an IllegalStateException, and I treat that as a feature rather than a nuisance — it surfaces a genuine data integrity problem instead of silently dropping a record. When duplicates are legitimately expected I switch to the three-argument form and supply a merge function.

The senior point I mention is to be deliberate about nulls and the map type: toMap throws if a value is null, and the default HashMap has no ordering, so when I need a specific map implementation or ordering I pass the fourth map-supplier argument. For an id-keyed lookup, uniqueness is the contract, so the plain two-argument form is both correct and intention-revealing.
